hero.title: Stabilize what is
hero.intro: A focused engagement for teams with a live digital product that has become unstable, delayed, fragile to release, or difficult to maintain.

overview.heading: Your product works. Delivery does not.
overview.body: We examine the product and delivery system, agree the critical scope with you, correct that scope, and leave your team with a prioritized recovery roadmap. A rescue is not an open-ended rebuild.

symptoms.title: Recurring production bugs
symptoms.description: The same failures return, fixes create regressions, or confidence in releases is falling.

symptoms.title: A fragile release process
symptoms.description: Deployments are manual, risky, poorly observed, or dependent on one person.

symptoms.title: A stalled roadmap
symptoms.description: Technical debt and unclear ownership make otherwise valuable features difficult to ship.

symptoms.title: A difficult handover
symptoms.description: A developer or technical cofounder has left and the incoming team needs a dependable path forward.

symptoms.title: Weak product visibility
symptoms.description: Monitoring, diagnostics, or operational documentation are not strong enough to explain failures.

symptoms.title: A temporary senior gap
symptoms.description: The internal team needs experienced engineering capacity to diagnose and unblock delivery.

pricingSection.heading: Two clear ways to begin.
pricingSection.body: Start with a paid assessment when the critical scope is not yet clear, or move into a bounded rescue sprint when the problem and access are ready.

packages.name: Rescue Assessment
packages.description: Choose this when the symptoms are clear but the critical technical scope is not.
packages.detail: Includes a focused assessment, risk map, recommended critical scope, and fixed implementation proposal. The fee is credited to a Rescue Sprint accepted within 14 days.

packages.name: Product Rescue Sprint
packages.description: Choose this when the problem, access, and critical outcome are ready to be bounded.
packages.detail: Includes the assessment, one agreed critical correction, verification, technical handover, and a prioritized recovery roadmap.

deliverablesSection.heading: A correction and a path forward.
deliverablesSection.body: The engagement stays anchored to an agreed critical scope. Broader implementation becomes a separate, deliberate decision.

deliverables.title: Technical assessment
deliverables.description: A focused review of the agreed product areas, delivery risks, and evidence available to the team.

deliverables.title: Critical-scope correction
deliverables.description: Implementation work on the specific high-priority scope agreed after assessment.

deliverables.title: Verification and handover
deliverables.description: Evidence that the agreed correction behaves as intended, plus a clear explanation for your team.

deliverables.title: Recovery roadmap
deliverables.description: A prioritized next-step plan separating urgent risks, stabilization work, and later improvements.

processSection.heading: Evidence before assumptions.
processSection.body: We start with the business impact, trace the relevant system, and keep the correction bounded to what both sides approve.

process.title: Understand
process.description: Confirm the business impact, access, constraints, and critical product area.

process.title: Assess
process.description: Trace the relevant system and delivery path using available evidence.

process.title: Prioritize
process.description: Agree the critical correction, boundaries, acceptance evidence, and next-step risks.

process.title: Correct
process.description: Implement and verify the agreed critical scope without silently expanding it.

process.title: Hand over
process.description: Explain the work and deliver a prioritized recovery roadmap.

fitSection.heading: Clear boundaries protect the outcome.
fitSection.body: A rescue works best when there is a live product, a concrete problem, and access to the people and systems needed to investigate it.

goodFit: You have a live product and a specific stability or delivery problem.
Your team can provide legitimate access to the relevant code, systems, and decision-makers.
You want an evidence-led plan before committing to a larger rebuild.
badFit: You need a full new product disguised as a short rescue.
The request depends on intrusive testing without written authorization.
You need guaranteed outcomes before the product and evidence can be assessed.
scopeNote: The exact scope, schedule, access requirements, and fee are confirmed after an initial conversation. Full implementation beyond the agreed correction and ongoing maintenance are separate engagements.

cta.title: Bring the product problem into focus.
cta.body: Tell us what is failing, what it is blocking, and what your team has already tried. We will respond with the right next step.
cta.label: Start a rescue conversation
